:::{#exr-flat-point}

#### Differentiate a quadratic

A [flat point](#def-flat-point) of a function is where its [derivative](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-derivative) is zero.
To see what that means, take a simple function with a minimum,
the quadratic $f(w) = w^2 - 4w + 7$,
whose graph is a [parabola](algebra.qmd#def-parabola).
The next exercises use it to find where $f$ is flat
and to compare a linear prediction of a nearby value with the exact value.

Differentiate $f$.

:::
